extraction.synopsis: In the harbour town of Corvel Quay, lamp-keeper Tomas Hale shows his apprentice Ines Varro that the page of the Salt Ledger for the night of the Gannet wreck, nine years ago, has been cut out. Their friend Bram Ostrow, a Guild journeyman, hears that Tomas asked Guild master Sabine Oake to reopen the inquiry and was refused. Odile Marr, master of the ship Kestrel and a survivor of the Gannet, arrives and asks to speak with Tomas. Tomas tells Ines that on the night of the wreck someone with a key was inside the locked lamp room, and that only the keeper and the Guild master hold keys.

extraction.synopsis: Nine years before the main story, Tomas Hale waits at Corvel Quay for his twelve-year-old daughter Livia, who is sailing home on the Gannet. In a storm the harbour lamp goes out; Tomas runs up the tower and finds the lamp room locked with someone crouching inside behind a lantern, but by the time he fetches his key the room is empty and the Gannet has struck the rocks. Eleven of thirty-four aboard survive, among them the mate Odile Marr, and the sisters of Brannoc Abbey nurse them. Livia is never found; after her green shawl turns up below the abbey the Guild enters her among the drowned, and Tomas keeps his suspicion about the lantern from the Guild master.

extraction.synopsis: Tomas and Ines climb the cliff stair to Brannoc Abbey to read the abbey's uncut fair copy of the Salt Ledger, but the archivist Sister Wren shows them that every book from the year of the wreck is under the Abbess's seal. After supper Tomas gives Ines the brass key to the lamp room and tells her to give it to no one, not even Master Oake. He walks out to the gate in the fog and is found dead at the foot of the stair. Bram Ostrow appears from the beach path saying he came to help, and Captain Fenn of the town watch rules the death an accident, which Ines does not believe.

extraction.synopsis: At Tomas's burial in Corvel Quay, Master Sabine Oake announces that the Guild will give the lamp to a senior keeper rather than to Ines. On the harbour wall Sister Wren reveals that she is Livia Hale, Tomas's daughter, who washed up below Brannoc Abbey after the wreck with no memory and was raised by the sisters under a new name. She adds that a tall grey woman, whom she now recognises as Master Oake, came asking whether any child had survived the Gannet, and Sister Agathe lied to protect her. Bram Ostrow then demands the lamp room key for Master Oake, who has promised him the keepership; he knocks Livia down and tears the key from Ines's neck, and Ines understands he is now her enemy.

extraction.synopsis: Livia breaks the Abbess's seal on the abbey's fair copy of the Salt Ledger, whose Keys Drawn column shows that Sabine Oake drew the master's key at six o'clock on the night of the wreck. At the watch house Odile Marr tells Captain Fenn she saw the master's grey barge leaving the dark lamp tower that night. Confronted in the Guild hall, Sabine Oake confesses she put out the lamp to drown an auditor who would have exposed her theft from the Guild's accounts, and Bram Ostrow confesses he was grappling with Tomas for the key at the top of the stair when Tomas fell. Fenn arrests both, with the key still in Bram's pocket, and that evening Ines and Livia light the harbour lamp together.
